title: Sensitive Data Catalog + Query‑Safe Logging + Access Provenance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Build a sensitivity-aware observability pipeline that classifies PII at the source (tracing hooks and log/metric emitters), enforces query-safe logging transforms in the ingestion pipeline, and adds role-scoped access provenance and audit trails in the Console. Rationale: current observability data can leak tenant or user PII into dashboards and long-term storage. We need a pragmatic approach that balances searchability for debugging with legal/compliance constraints and low operational overhead. This ticket implements the core platform pieces (catalog, pipeline transforms, storage changes, and access logging) required for follow-on per-team policies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sensitivity catalog service introduced: canonical schema for sensitivity labels (public, internal, sensitive_personal, pii_hashed, pii_masked) with versioning and rule sources (runtime hook, ingestion classifier, manual overrides).
2) Tracing hooks updated to annotate spans with sensitivity labels and a stable field 'sensitivity.label' that ingestion can trust when present. Backwards-compatibility mode if label absent.

3) Ingestion pipeline (metrics/logs/traces) implements query-safe transforms: tokenization of PII values into keyed HMAC placeholders, field-level masking for common PII patterns, and a configurable policy to retain original hashed tokens for correlation for a configurable retention tier.

4) Console RBAC additions: 'observability/see_sensitive' permission gated behind SSO groups; UI surfaces limited views for users without permission; requests to sensitive views are logged to an immutable audit stream with requestor, reason, and sample query.

5) Retention enforcement: retention tiers (ephemeral=7d, short=30d, standard=365d, long=730d) applied by sensitivity label with automated purging jobs and a migration plan for historical data older than new thresholds.
6) End-to-end tests and load tests demonstrating <5% ingestion latency regression at 99th percentile for normal workloads and acceptable throughput impact for high-volume tenants.
7) Security review completed and documented; KMS-backed key usage for token HMAC salting and field encryption is validated.
tasks: Design sensitivity catalog data model and API (Research & Product review)
Add sensitivity annotation hooks to runtime tracers (python/go/node SDKs)
Implement ingestion classifier stage with regex & ML-backed heuristics for fallback labeling
Build query-safe transform module (HMAC tokenization + mask templates) in pipeline
Extend object store schema to store masked + hashed token columns separately
Console: add permission checks, audit logging endpoints, and minimal UI affordances for sensitive-filtered views
Retention worker: implement tiered purging jobs and dry-run migration tooling
Integration tests: unit, e2e tracing->ingest->console, and perf benchmark harness
Document runbooks for incident response when sensitive data is discovered in older stores
updates: 2026-03-06 - Kickoff: Met with PM (Mariana Silva) and Security (Lukas Mayer). Agreed scope and initial retention tiers. Decided to prefer keyed HMAC tokens over reversible encryption for correlation without revealing raw PII.

2026-03-08 - Design review: Sensitivity catalog schema v0.1 ready; added fields for 'source', 'confidence', and 'rule_id'. Product asked for manual override workflow for support engineers — scoped as follow-up small ticket.

2026-03-09 - Eng sync: Jonah started tracer changes (node + python). Tracing team requested a minimal hook API to avoid SDK churn; agreed to expose 'setSensitivity(label, metadata)' with optional TTL.

2026-03-11 - Prototype: Ingestion transform implemented in staging using HMAC(token, tenant_key). Observed ~3% p99 latency increase on small cluster. Planning to optimize parallelism and batch transforms.
2026-03-12 - Security: Submitted design to security review board. Added explicit KMS key rotation notes and audit log retention requirements.
2026-03-13 - Blocker identified: historical cluster has mixed schema; need migration plan to add hashed_token column. Jonah to draft migration and dry-run steps by 2026-03-18.
